jobs.title: Data Analyst II, Tech
jobs.description:
About The Role And Team

We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled Data Analyst to join the Mobility Customer Experience Analytics team and become a key player in shaping the future of our business! In this high-impact role, you will apply your strategic and analytical prowess to drive data-driven decisions across critical elements of our mobility ecosystem, with a specific focus on growth bets, new product launches, and airports and venues. You will leverage our broad suite of ETL and data automation tools to build lasting data infrastructure while nimbly finding immediate insights that improve the business. This is an opportunity to define our analytical priorities and own the North Star metrics that measure the success of our growth bets and new product launches.

You will be at the forefront of shaping our customer support experience design and tracking its impact across both traditional and cutting-edge GenAI-powered support channels. By designing deep-dive analyses, unearthing invaluable insights, and collaborating cross-functionally, you will uncover opportunities to streamline our user-facing support experience and enhance the tech we use to deliver it, ultimately driving groundbreaking solutions and significant impact for both the business and our users.

What You'll Do

Own North Star metrics and targets to measure and deliver against the Mobility Customer Experience strategy.
Perform deep-dive analysis and drive business decisions by developing testable hypotheses and designing experiments that clearly quantify the impact of new product launches, growth bets, and airport/venue operations through rigorous ROI analysis.
Evaluate and shape customer support design, establishing rigorous impact tracking across both traditional support workflows and GenAI-powered support experiences.
Translate ambiguous questions into data-driven recommendations that identify opportunities to streamline the user-facing support experience and advocate for customer-first changes to our products, app features, and support policies.
Create and manage intuitive, self-service data products, dashboards, and reporting frameworks to empower non-technical users, business leaders, and cross-functional partners.
Develop an in-depth understanding of business performance and build compelling, executive-level communications to share strategic insights and influence senior leadership across the Mobility ecosystem.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Operations, and Finance teams to implement data-backed recommendations, execute root-cause analyses, and drive operational efficiency.
Write complex SQL queries and leverage data modeling to extract, manipulate, and transform raw data into stable, "single source of truth" architectures.
Use Python and modern LLM-powered coding tools for data transformation, automation, and model development, deepening the team's ability to rapidly draw actionable insights from complex datasets.
Potentially lead junior analysts and play a leadership role in developing, standardizing, and elevating the team's analytical tools, frameworks, and processes.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Analytics, or a related field
3+ years of experience in analytics, business intelligence, data engineering, or a within a similar role
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, R, and SQL with proven ability to write and understand complex queries

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated experience using LLM-based coding and analytics tools to drive business outcomes
Advanced SQL skills.
High technical proficiency in common analytics & reporting tools (e.g., Tableau, Google Data Studio, Google Sheets/Excel).
Skill in building intuitive, self-service tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker, Streamlit) for non-technical users and business leaders.
Experience in Python
Experience working with customer support or customer insights.
Advanced data analysis skills leading to actionable recommendations.
Experience in leading high-visibility projects and influencing others in a cross-functional team environment
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present complex data insights to both technical and non-technical audiences
Strong sense of ownership and accountability
Curious, self-directed, and impact-driven-you chase high-impact problems to deliver solutions.
Comfortable with ambiguity and switching contexts in a fast-moving environment
Experience in communicating with and presenting to senior leaders.
Strong storytelling ability: Distilling exciting and hard-to-find insights into a compelling, concise data story.
Comfort in working with ambiguity in a fast-paced environment
Experience in data extraction, wrangling, and building pipelines.
Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset
Highly self-motivated, proactive, and able to drive projects independently.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Detail-oriented mindset, with a focus on accuracy, efficiency, and process standardization.

For New York City, NY-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $135,000 per year - USD $150,000 per year.

For San Francisco, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $135,000 per year - USD $150,000 per year.

For all US locations, you will be eligible to participate in Uber's bonus program, and may be offered an equity award & other types of comp. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan. You will also be eligible for various benefits.

Ready to Ride?

This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook - it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves - we'd love to hear from you.

You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.

Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. Unless approved for full remote work, employees must spend at least 50% of their time in-office. Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full-time in-office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this role's requirements.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. jobs.title: Global Data Science Lead
jobs.description:
Veeva is building the industry cloud for Life Sciences through software, data, AI, and business consulting working together. Learn more about our products, vision, values, and status as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) on our website.

Consulting is changing, and we’re not like other firms. Launched in 2019, Veeva Business Consulting has grown quickly and organically to over 500 global experts who combine deep domain knowledge with innovative technology to help Life Sciences companies work in a more efficient and connected way.

We are growing aggressively as we look towards 2030. We are seeking great people to help shape the future of the industry with the world’s leading software, data, AI, and expertise at their back.

The Role

The Global Analytics Business Consulting Team applies data science and AI to help customers turn commercial, medical, and regulatory data into action. We are seeking a Global Data Science Lead that will support execution of the Data Science AI strategy within this team. This role will lead a group of data scientists, AI/ML engineers, and analysts, and partners with Global Analytics leadership to turn strategy into delivery — applying advanced analytics, machine learning, and generative AI/LLM techniques to life sciences data.

What You'll Do

Lead the Data Science function within the Global Analytics Team, in line with Veeva's Analytics Business Consulting goals
Lead, mentor, and inspire a team of data scientists, AI/ML engineers, and analysts within the Global Analytics Team
Partner with Global Analytics leadership to translate the broader Data Science AI strategy into team priorities and delivery plans
Own global methodology – model management, observability, testing, and deployment
Foster collaboration between consulting, data science, and engineering teams to ensure seamless integration of AI-driven data solutions
Oversee the design and implementation of advanced analytics, machine learning, and generative AI/LLM models within the Global Analytics Team's scope of work
Ensure the development and maintenance of robust, scalable, and efficient data and AI infrastructure supporting Global Analytics Team deliverables
Collaborate with cross-functional consulting teams to understand customer business requirements and translate them into AI-native, data-driven solutions
Work with product and business stakeholders to surface opportunities for applying AI within Global Analytics Team engagements
Enforce best practices for data quality, security, governance, and responsible AI use within the team
Implement and maintain rigorous testing procedures to validate the accuracy and reliability of data, ML, and AI models

Requirements

Ph.D. in Economics, Machine Learning, Applied Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, or other quantitative discipline with 5+ years of relevant industry experience, or equivalent M.S. with 8+ years of relevant demonstrable research experience
Experience with the Life Sciences industry and applying analytics and AI/ML to related data sets
Hands-on experience building or deploying LLM-based systems (prompt engineering, RAG, agentic workflows, or fine-tuning). Advanced, in-depth specialization in data science and AI techniques including classification, pattern recognition, clustering, feature analysis, NLP, fuzzy matching, sentiment analysis, A/B testing, active/adaptive learning
Proven leadership of teams of 10+ people
Intellectual curiosity, along with excellent problem-solving and quantitative skills, including the ability to disaggregate issues, identify root causes, and recommend solutions, even in situations with non-standard problems
Excellent oral and written communication skills with the ability to effectively explain complex technical and AI-driven solutions to other team members and clients
Must be comfortable with changing requirements and priorities
Must be results-oriented and able to move forward without complete information and with minimal supervision

Nice to Have

Advanced experience with AWS, Snowflake, or Databricks
Data pipeline building skills
Product development experience
Experience with LLM orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex) or vector databases
Experience designing AI-native products or workflows, not just adding AI to existing systems

Interviewing with Veeva

We value your time and believe in a transparent hiring process. Here is the process you can expect.

Follow the application process and submit your resume.
If moving to the interview stage, our process is as follows:
A conversation with the hiring manager
A personality assessment
A practical case exercise
A final conversation with our group's Senior Leader

Once all interviews are complete, the manager will be in touch with a final decision.

Perks & Benefits

Medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance
Flexible PTO and company paid holidays
Retirement programs
1% charitable giving program
Unrivaled career progression in a fast-growing, global team
Veeva is a Work Anywhere company. You can work from home or the office on any given day

Compensation

Base pay: $120,000 - $250,000
The salary range listed here has been provided to comply with local regulations and represents a potential base salary range for this role. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range above or below, depending on experience and location. We look at compensation for each individual and base our offer on your unique qualifications, experience, and expected contributions. This position may also be eligible for other types of compensation in addition to base salary, such as variable bonus and/or stock bonus.

Veeva’s headquarters is located in the San Francisco Bay Area with offices in more than 15 countries around the world.

Veeva is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, national origin or ancestry, age, disability, marital status, pregnancy, protected veteran status, protected genetic information, political affiliation, or any other characteristics protected by local laws, regulations, or ordinances. If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability or special need when applying for a role or in our recruitment process, please contact us at talent_accommodations@veeva.com.

jobs.title: Clinical Solutions Engineer (Subject Matter Expert) - West Coast
jobs.description:
Do you bring hands-on next-generation sequencing (NGS) experience and an understanding of clinical laboratory operations? Have you helped a clinical laboratory navigate CAP/CLIA requirements and bring a new assay into routine use? Do you want to utilise your technical and clinical knowledge within a commercialised environment?

If this sounds like you and you are driven by purpose, join the SOPHiA GENETICS NORAM Sales team as a Clinical Solutions Engineer and enable us to make a positive impact on the outcomes for cancer and rare disease patients worldwide.

This is a field-based role. You'll work from a home office or travel across your territory for customer meetings, conferences and events.

We're looking for someone based in the United States, in the region spanning the West Coast through Texas. In most instances, we look for individuals already living in-territory, but welcome those actively relocating to the area.

Our Mission

We believe there is a smarter, more data-driven way to make decisions in healthcare and our cloud-native AI powered SOPHiA DDM Platform makes that vision a reality on a daily basis. You will have direct input to our mission to democratize data-driven medicine for the ultimate benefit of cancer and rare disease patients across the globe.

Your Mission

You'll help clinical laboratories make informed decisions about purchasing the SOPHiA GENETICS ecosystem, drawing on your hands-on NGS experience and understanding of laboratory operations, assay implementation and CAP/CLIA requirements. Working alongside sales colleagues, you'll use that knowledge to understand customers' needs, address their concerns and explain what adoption would mean for their laboratory. Your role is to build confidence in the buying decision, not to carry out the implementation.

The value you add

Build credibility with laboratory teams by connecting to their clinical, technical and operational needs.
Help prospective customers assess what adoption would involve, using your knowledge of assay implementation, validation and the path to routine use.
Address buying concerns about CAP/CLIA requirements, documentation and implementation timelines with an understanding of how clinical laboratories work.
Partner with sales colleagues to answer technical and operational questions and help customers move towards a confident, informed buying decision.

Requirements

We know that every background is different, but to be best set for success we see you bringing:

Hands-on wet-lab experience with NGS workflows in a clinical laboratory.
An understanding of how clinical laboratories operate beyond the bench, including the steps needed to introduce and validate a new assay.
Substantial exposure to CAP/CLIA requirements and inspection processes, with enough involvement to explain their practical impact on laboratory work.
Experience of assay implementation or validation that helps you understand the challenges laboratories face before going live.
Willingness to travel for a customer-facing role.

You do not need to have held a customer-facing role, or previously worked as an SME or field applications specialist, but it is helpful. A desire to work in a commercialsed environment as part of a sales and solutions team is critical.

Benefits

You will be joining an organization with the patient at the heart of every decision and action, driven by purpose as we pursue exponential growth.

For more information about our Benefits, Virtues, The Recruitment Process, our AI guide and stories from our team about what it's like to work at SOPHiA, view the full posting on our careers page.

Location: Remote - Home Office in Territory (West Coast)

Contract: Permanent

jobs.title: Manager, People Analytics & Data Science
jobs.description:
Position Summary

Mercury is building a connected, trusted people analytics capability that puts decision-ready data and insights in the hands of leaders when and where they need them. The Manager, People Analytics & Data Science will help build that capability from the data foundation through the leader experience.

This role will build reliable data pipelines and analytical datasets, establish trusted metric definitions, and deliver robust dashboards that enable self-service people data for Mercury leaders. The role will also conduct targeted research and advanced analysis—including predictive and AI-enabled methods where appropriate—to surface new insights on workforce risks, capacity, performance, productivity, and other priorities.

The successful candidate will combine technical depth with strong business judgment. They will be able to move from a business question to a data model, from a data model to a clear dashboard, and from an observed pattern to a well-supported recommendation. This is a builder role for someone who wants to make people data easier to trust, easier to use, and more useful in the flow of business decisions.

Geo-Salary Information

An in-person interview may be required during the hiring process

State specific pay scales for this role are as follows:

$128,136 to $252,194 (NJ, NY, WA, HI, AK, MD, CT, RI, MA)

$116,487 to $229,267 (NV, OR, AZ, CO, WY, TX, ND, MN, MO, IL, WI, FL, GA, MI, OH, VA, PA, DE, VT, NH, ME)

$104,839 to $206,340 (UT, ID, MT, NM, SD, NE, KS, OK, IA, AR, LA, MS, AL, TN, KY, IN, SC, NC, WV)

In CA: Typical hiring range is $171,148 to $209,181

The expected base salary for this position will vary depending on a number of factors, including relevant experience, skills and location.

Responsibilities

Data foundation and analytics engineering

Partner with data engineers to design, build, and maintain reliable data pipelines and analytical datasets that bring together people, organizational, operational, and business data from relevant sources.
Develop reusable data models, transformations, validation checks, documentation, and monitoring that support accurate and repeatable analysis.
Partner with HR Tech, Enterprise Data Science, Data & Analytics, Finance, and other technical teams on source systems, data architecture, integrations, access, and data quality.
Translate business and People questions into clear data requirements, grains, dimensions, logic, refresh expectations, and ownership.
Establish and maintain metric contracts that document definitions, calculation logic, sources, refresh cadence, interpretation, stewardship, and action path.
Improve the reliability, transparency, privacy, and usability of people data as Mercury evolves its HRIS and broader data ecosystem.

Dashboards and self-service people data

Own the end-to-end delivery of leader-facing people data products, from discovery and prioritization through launch, adoption, and iteration.
Build robust operational and executive dashboards that connect people metrics to business and workforce outcomes.
Deliver focused dashboard experiences that help leaders answer what changed, what may be contributing, and what action to take next.
Design for self-service by developing intuitive personas, access patterns, definitions, documentation, enablement, and feedback loops.
Embed relevant people insights into existing executive reporting and operating rhythms wherever possible rather than creating disconnected destinations.
Measure usage, trust, decision relevance, and adoption; use feedback and evidence to expand, refine, or retire products.

Research, advanced analytics, and predictive insight

Conduct targeted research and analysis on prioritized questions such as attrition risk, critical-role readiness, capacity constraints, workforce planning, manager effectiveness, performance, productivity, and AI-enabled work.
Apply exploratory analysis, statistical methods, experimentation, forecasting, segmentation, and predictive modeling as appropriate to the question and data quality.
Translate complex analysis into clear findings, limitations, implications, and recommendations for People and business leaders.
Design analyses with appropriate validation, explainability, privacy protections, and bias-awareness; treat models as decision support, not a substitute for accountable human judgment.
Develop repeatable approaches for research intake, hypothesis formation, analysis, peer review, storytelling, and follow-through.
Partner with stakeholders to connect analytical findings to decisions, interventions, and measures of impact.

Partnership and capability building

Build trusted relationships with People leaders, business leaders, Finance, HR Tech, Enterprise Data Science, and other partners.
Shape and maintain an analytics roadmap that balances foundational data work, self-service products, and targeted research.
Establish practical standards for data quality, versioning, testing, documentation, access, and responsible use of people data.
Help leaders and People partners build confidence and fluency in using people metrics and insights.
Lead through influence and contribute to a high-performing, collaborative People Ops, Tech & Analytics team.

What success looks like

Leaders can access trusted people metrics in the tools and business rhythms where decisions already happen.
Core dashboards are clear, adopted, well-governed, and connected to meaningful business questions.
Data pipelines, metric definitions, and analytical products are reliable enough to support recurring decisions—not just one-time requests.
Targeted research produces new, decision-relevant insight on priority workforce questions.
The team has a scalable roadmap for expanding self-service, predictive analysis, and future HRIS-enabled analytics.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree in data science, statistics, computer science, mathematics, engineering, economics, business analytics, or a related field

Experience

7+ years of experience in data science, people analytics, analytics engineering, business intelligence, data engineering, or a related field.
Experience with People Analytics, HR data, workforce planning, talent, compensation, performance, or organizational research.
Demonstrated experience building data pipelines, analytical datasets, data models, or other reusable analytics infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience developing dashboards or self-service analytics products for business stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience applying statistical analysis, experimentation, forecasting, segmentation, or predictive modeling to complex business questions.
Demonstrated ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to senior leaders and non-technical audiences.
Strong hands-on skills with SQL and Python or R, plus experience with modern data pipelines, transformation, testing, and analytical workflows.
Experience with data modeling, semantic layers, BI tools, cloud data platforms, version control, and production-quality documentation.
Strong foundation in statistics, experimental design, causal reasoning, predictive modeling, and model evaluation.

Knowledge and Skills:

Able to distinguish between a reporting need, a diagnostic question, and a research or modeling question—and choose an appropriately rigorous solution.
Product-minded and user-centered: starts with the decision and designs the data experience around the user.
Strong storyteller who can make complex analysis clear, precise, and actionable without overstating certainty.
Highly collaborative, curious, pragmatic, and comfortable working across business and technical teams.
Strong judgment and discretion when handling confidential, sensitive, or personally identifiable People data.
Comfortable using AI and collaboration tools to improve productivity while applying responsible-use principles.
Able to build in ambiguity, establish standards without over-engineering, and continuously improve the quality of the work.

About The Company

Why choose a career at Mercury?

At Mercury, we have been guided by our purpose to help people reduce risk and overcome unexpected events for more than 60 years. We are one team with a common goal to help others. Everyone needs insurance and we can’t imagine a world without it.

Our team will encourage you to grow, make time to have fun, and work together to make great things happen. We embrace the strengths and values of each team member. We believe in having diverse perspectives where everyone is included, to serve customers from all walks of life.

We care about our people, and we mean it. We reward our talented professionals with a competitive salary, bonus potential, and a variety of benefits to help our team members reach their health, retirement, and professional goals.

Learn more about us here: https://www.mercuryinsurance.com/about/careers

Perks And Benefits

We offer many great benefits, including:

Competitive compensation
Flexibility to work from anywhere in the United States for most positions
Paid time off (vacation time, sick time, 9 paid Company holidays, volunteer hours)
Incentive bonus programs (potential for holiday bonus, referral bonus, and performance-based bonus)
Medical, dental, vision, life, and pet insurance
401 (k) retirement savings plan with company match
Engaging work environment
Promotional opportunities
Education assistance
Professional and personal development opportunities
Company recognition program
Health and wellbeing resources, including free mental wellbeing therapy/coaching sessions, child and eldercare resources, and more

This position is covered by a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) with SEIU.

This position was originally posted to ratified STC SEUI CBA members from 10/6/26 – 10/14/26. The position is now available to be filled by internal candidates that are not members of the ratified Bargaining Unit or External candidates to Sharp.

What You Will Do

The primary functions of the Laboratory Assistant I are specimen collection, specimen handling and transport, specimen processing– including reference laboratory specimen processing and microbiology specimen processing clerical support, inventory monitoring, and assisting the Clinical Laboratory Scientist in the performance of automated, semi-automated and manual procedures in the clinical laboratory. 

Required Qualifications

Other Meets education requirements for California CPT Certification.
California Certified Phlebotomy Technician I (CPT I) Certificate - CA Department of Public Health; OR California Certified Phlebotomy Technician II (CPT II) Certificate - CA Department of Public Health -REQUIRED

Preferred Qualifications

Associate's Degree in life science courses or equivalent.
1 Year relevant work experience in a laboratory.
Minimum 6 months Phlebotomy experience.

Essential Functions

The position characteristics reflect the most important duties, responsibilities and competencies considered necessary to perform the essential functions of the job in a fully competent manner. They should not be considered as a detailed description of all the work requirements of the position. The characteristics of the position and standards of performance may be changed by TCMC with or without prior notice based on the needs of the organization. Maintains a safe, clean working environment, including unit based safety and infection control requirements. Perform specimen collections, includes venipuncture and capillary sticks. Process specimens received in the laboratory. This task includes specimen transport, handling, sorting, requisition entry, distribution of specimens to all laboratory sections. Centrifuge and aliquot specimens to appropriate containers. Enter blood culture bottles on the blood culture instrumentation. Answer the telephone, triage calls appropriately, take appropriate messages; review pending logs; locate samples for add on orders; look up patient reports on computer and give results to clinicians where appropriate. Assists in the Reception/Triage area of the Lab, as needed. Order tests in the LIS. Contact nursing units or physician’s offices to verify confusing incomplete or confusing orders or sample problems. Under the direct observation of the Clinical Laboratory Scientist, set up and load tests on instruments or procedures as determined by the section lead. Under the direct observation of the Clinical Laboratory Scientist, perform limited function checks and preventative maintenance on instruments and equipment. Take inventory of reagents and supplies and restock when needed; put away supplies as they are received. Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Knowledge and ability to use medical terminology, preferred.
Excellent professional communication and interpersonal skills are essential.

jobs.title: Chief College Laboratory Technician (Classroom) - Hunter-Bellevue School of Nursing, Hunter College
jobs.description:
Directs and trains other laboratory or technical personnel under general supervision and performs highly specialized work requiring significant theoretical knowledge, scientific and technical expertise, professional judgment, and insight in one of the fields of laboratory or applied science. 

May oversee multiple laboratories in a single department, or laboratories in multiple departments with a significant number of technicians. Highly specialized work may include development of research designs and fabrication, modification, repair, maintenance and operation of highly complex research or technical equipment.

Job Title Name: Chief College Laboratory Technician

CONTRACT TITLE
Chief College Laboratory Technician

FLSA
Exempt

CAMPUS SPECIFIC INFORMATION
The Hunter-Bellevue School of Nursing at Hunter College is the flagship nursing school of the City University of New York (CUNY) and cultivates collaborative nurse leaders promoting wellness and championing health equity in local and global communities through excellence in education, research, scholarship, and advocacy. The School of Nursing invites highly motivated applicants for the position of Chief College Lab Technician.
POSITION DETAILS:
Reporting to the Dean, the Chief College Lab Technician will:
•    Manage the day-to-day operations of the nursing labs, including scheduling, equipment maintenance, and inventory control.
•    Train and supervise lab personnel.
•    Enforce and implement safety protocols. 
•    Troubleshoot hardware and software issues and coordinates the maintenance and system upgrades of technology/equipment.
•    Support faculty and students in clinical teaching and simulation-based learning in nursing lab settings. 
•    Identify equipment and technology for clinical teaching and simulation-based learning.
•    Provide faculty training regarding technology and equipment.
•    Maintain currency and proficiency in related technology and software.
•    Ensure adherence to CUNY, state, and federal regulations for lab operations and safety.
•    Develop lab policies and procedures.
•    Work evenings and weekends as needed.
•    Other duties that align with the school’s mission and strategic goals. 

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
High School Diploma with a minimum of twelve years' related experience. Additional education may be used to meet the experience requirement: an Associate degree may be substituted for two years experience, a Bachelor's degree may be substituted for four years experience, and a Master's degree in an area appropriate to the duties to be performed may be substituted for an additional one year's experience. This position requires a high level of technical expertise.

OTHER QUALIFICATIONS
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
•    Bachelor’s degree or higher in nursing.
•    New York State license as a registered nurse required or following hire. 
•    Experience in a nursing or simulation lab beneficial.
•    Strong knowledge of infection control, safety, and quality procedures.
•    Proficiency in nursing skills and technology.
•    Excellent organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
•    Expertise with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint and other software systems.
•    Ability to work in a fast-paced, educational environment with attention to detail.

COMPENSATION
Salary commensurate with education and experience ($102,508 - $111,459).

CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development.

BENEFITS
CUNY offers a comprehensive benefits package to employees and eligible dependents based on job title and classification. Employees are also offered pension and Tax-Deferred Savings Plans. Part-time employees must meet a weekly or semester work hour criteria to be eligible for health benefits. Health benefits are also extended to retirees who meet the eligibility criteria.

CLOSING DATE
The search will remain open until the position is filled. The committee will begin reviewing complete applications on Oct. 19, 2026. Applications submitted after the deadline will only be considered if the position/s remain open after initial round.

JOB SEARCH CATEGORY
CUNY Job Posting: Support Staff

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY
CUNY encourages people with disabilities, minorities, veterans and women to apply. At CUNY, Italian Americans are also included among our protected groups. Applicants and employees will not be discriminated against on the basis of any legally protected category, including sexual orientation or gender identity. EEO/AA/Vet/Disability Employer.

new_jobs.title: Data Analyst II, Tech
new_jobs.description:
About The Role And Team

We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled Data Analyst to join the Mobility Customer Experience Analytics team and become a key player in shaping the future of our business! In this high-impact role, you will apply your strategic and analytical prowess to drive data-driven decisions across critical elements of our mobility ecosystem, with a specific focus on growth bets, new product launches, and airports and venues. You will leverage our broad suite of ETL and data automation tools to build lasting data infrastructure while nimbly finding immediate insights that improve the business. This is an opportunity to define our analytical priorities and own the North Star metrics that measure the success of our growth bets and new product launches.

You will be at the forefront of shaping our customer support experience design and tracking its impact across both traditional and cutting-edge GenAI-powered support channels. By designing deep-dive analyses, unearthing invaluable insights, and collaborating cross-functionally, you will uncover opportunities to streamline our user-facing support experience and enhance the tech we use to deliver it, ultimately driving groundbreaking solutions and significant impact for both the business and our users.

What You'll Do

Own North Star metrics and targets to measure and deliver against the Mobility Customer Experience strategy.
Perform deep-dive analysis and drive business decisions by developing testable hypotheses and designing experiments that clearly quantify the impact of new product launches, growth bets, and airport/venue operations through rigorous ROI analysis.
Evaluate and shape customer support design, establishing rigorous impact tracking across both traditional support workflows and GenAI-powered support experiences.
Translate ambiguous questions into data-driven recommendations that identify opportunities to streamline the user-facing support experience and advocate for customer-first changes to our products, app features, and support policies.
Create and manage intuitive, self-service data products, dashboards, and reporting frameworks to empower non-technical users, business leaders, and cross-functional partners.
Develop an in-depth understanding of business performance and build compelling, executive-level communications to share strategic insights and influence senior leadership across the Mobility ecosystem.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Operations, and Finance teams to implement data-backed recommendations, execute root-cause analyses, and drive operational efficiency.
Write complex SQL queries and leverage data modeling to extract, manipulate, and transform raw data into stable, "single source of truth" architectures.
Use Python and modern LLM-powered coding tools for data transformation, automation, and model development, deepening the team's ability to rapidly draw actionable insights from complex datasets.
Potentially lead junior analysts and play a leadership role in developing, standardizing, and elevating the team's analytical tools, frameworks, and processes.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Analytics, or a related field
3+ years of experience in analytics, business intelligence, data engineering, or a within a similar role
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, R, and SQL with proven ability to write and understand complex queries

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated experience using LLM-based coding and analytics tools to drive business outcomes
Advanced SQL skills.
High technical proficiency in common analytics & reporting tools (e.g., Tableau, Google Data Studio, Google Sheets/Excel).
Skill in building intuitive, self-service tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker, Streamlit) for non-technical users and business leaders.
Experience in Python
Experience working with customer support or customer insights.
Advanced data analysis skills leading to actionable recommendations.
Experience in leading high-visibility projects and influencing others in a cross-functional team environment
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present complex data insights to both technical and non-technical audiences
Strong sense of ownership and accountability
Curious, self-directed, and impact-driven-you chase high-impact problems to deliver solutions.
Comfortable with ambiguity and switching contexts in a fast-moving environment
Experience in communicating with and presenting to senior leaders.
Strong storytelling ability: Distilling exciting and hard-to-find insights into a compelling, concise data story.
Comfort in working with ambiguity in a fast-paced environment
Experience in data extraction, wrangling, and building pipelines.
Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset
Highly self-motivated, proactive, and able to drive projects independently.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Detail-oriented mindset, with a focus on accuracy, efficiency, and process standardization.

For New York City, NY-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $135,000 per year - USD $150,000 per year.

For San Francisco, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $135,000 per year - USD $150,000 per year.

For all US locations, you will be eligible to participate in Uber's bonus program, and may be offered an equity award & other types of comp. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan. You will also be eligible for various benefits.

Ready to Ride?

This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook - it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves - we'd love to hear from you.

You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.

Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. Unless approved for full remote work, employees must spend at least 50% of their time in-office. Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full-time in-office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this role's requirements.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. new_jobs.title: Global Data Science Lead
new_jobs.description:
Veeva is building the industry cloud for Life Sciences through software, data, AI, and business consulting working together. Learn more about our products, vision, values, and status as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) on our website.

Consulting is changing, and we’re not like other firms. Launched in 2019, Veeva Business Consulting has grown quickly and organically to over 500 global experts who combine deep domain knowledge with innovative technology to help Life Sciences companies work in a more efficient and connected way.

We are growing aggressively as we look towards 2030. We are seeking great people to help shape the future of the industry with the world’s leading software, data, AI, and expertise at their back.

The Role

The Global Analytics Business Consulting Team applies data science and AI to help customers turn commercial, medical, and regulatory data into action. We are seeking a Global Data Science Lead that will support execution of the Data Science AI strategy within this team. This role will lead a group of data scientists, AI/ML engineers, and analysts, and partners with Global Analytics leadership to turn strategy into delivery — applying advanced analytics, machine learning, and generative AI/LLM techniques to life sciences data.

What You'll Do

Lead the Data Science function within the Global Analytics Team, in line with Veeva's Analytics Business Consulting goals
Lead, mentor, and inspire a team of data scientists, AI/ML engineers, and analysts within the Global Analytics Team
Partner with Global Analytics leadership to translate the broader Data Science AI strategy into team priorities and delivery plans
Own global methodology – model management, observability, testing, and deployment
Foster collaboration between consulting, data science, and engineering teams to ensure seamless integration of AI-driven data solutions
Oversee the design and implementation of advanced analytics, machine learning, and generative AI/LLM models within the Global Analytics Team's scope of work
Ensure the development and maintenance of robust, scalable, and efficient data and AI infrastructure supporting Global Analytics Team deliverables
Collaborate with cross-functional consulting teams to understand customer business requirements and translate them into AI-native, data-driven solutions
Work with product and business stakeholders to surface opportunities for applying AI within Global Analytics Team engagements
Enforce best practices for data quality, security, governance, and responsible AI use within the team
Implement and maintain rigorous testing procedures to validate the accuracy and reliability of data, ML, and AI models

Requirements

Ph.D. in Economics, Machine Learning, Applied Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, or other quantitative discipline with 5+ years of relevant industry experience, or equivalent M.S. with 8+ years of relevant demonstrable research experience
Experience with the Life Sciences industry and applying analytics and AI/ML to related data sets
Hands-on experience building or deploying LLM-based systems (prompt engineering, RAG, agentic workflows, or fine-tuning). Advanced, in-depth specialization in data science and AI techniques including classification, pattern recognition, clustering, feature analysis, NLP, fuzzy matching, sentiment analysis, A/B testing, active/adaptive learning
Proven leadership of teams of 10+ people
Intellectual curiosity, along with excellent problem-solving and quantitative skills, including the ability to disaggregate issues, identify root causes, and recommend solutions, even in situations with non-standard problems
Excellent oral and written communication skills with the ability to effectively explain complex technical and AI-driven solutions to other team members and clients
Must be comfortable with changing requirements and priorities
Must be results-oriented and able to move forward without complete information and with minimal supervision

Nice to Have

Advanced experience with AWS, Snowflake, or Databricks
Data pipeline building skills
Product development experience
Experience with LLM orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex) or vector databases
Experience designing AI-native products or workflows, not just adding AI to existing systems

Interviewing with Veeva

We value your time and believe in a transparent hiring process. Here is the process you can expect.

Follow the application process and submit your resume.
If moving to the interview stage, our process is as follows:
A conversation with the hiring manager
A personality assessment
A practical case exercise
A final conversation with our group's Senior Leader

Once all interviews are complete, the manager will be in touch with a final decision.

Perks & Benefits

Medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance
Flexible PTO and company paid holidays
Retirement programs
1% charitable giving program
Unrivaled career progression in a fast-growing, global team
Veeva is a Work Anywhere company. You can work from home or the office on any given day

Compensation

Base pay: $120,000 - $250,000
The salary range listed here has been provided to comply with local regulations and represents a potential base salary range for this role. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range above or below, depending on experience and location. We look at compensation for each individual and base our offer on your unique qualifications, experience, and expected contributions. This position may also be eligible for other types of compensation in addition to base salary, such as variable bonus and/or stock bonus.

Veeva’s headquarters is located in the San Francisco Bay Area with offices in more than 15 countries around the world.

Veeva is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, national origin or ancestry, age, disability, marital status, pregnancy, protected veteran status, protected genetic information, political affiliation, or any other characteristics protected by local laws, regulations, or ordinances. If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability or special need when applying for a role or in our recruitment process, please contact us at talent_accommodations@veeva.com.

new_jobs.title: Clinical Solutions Engineer (Subject Matter Expert) - West Coast
new_jobs.description:
Do you bring hands-on next-generation sequencing (NGS) experience and an understanding of clinical laboratory operations? Have you helped a clinical laboratory navigate CAP/CLIA requirements and bring a new assay into routine use? Do you want to utilise your technical and clinical knowledge within a commercialised environment?

If this sounds like you and you are driven by purpose, join the SOPHiA GENETICS NORAM Sales team as a Clinical Solutions Engineer and enable us to make a positive impact on the outcomes for cancer and rare disease patients worldwide.

This is a field-based role. You'll work from a home office or travel across your territory for customer meetings, conferences and events.

We're looking for someone based in the United States, in the region spanning the West Coast through Texas. In most instances, we look for individuals already living in-territory, but welcome those actively relocating to the area.

Our Mission

We believe there is a smarter, more data-driven way to make decisions in healthcare and our cloud-native AI powered SOPHiA DDM Platform makes that vision a reality on a daily basis. You will have direct input to our mission to democratize data-driven medicine for the ultimate benefit of cancer and rare disease patients across the globe.

Your Mission

You'll help clinical laboratories make informed decisions about purchasing the SOPHiA GENETICS ecosystem, drawing on your hands-on NGS experience and understanding of laboratory operations, assay implementation and CAP/CLIA requirements. Working alongside sales colleagues, you'll use that knowledge to understand customers' needs, address their concerns and explain what adoption would mean for their laboratory. Your role is to build confidence in the buying decision, not to carry out the implementation.

The value you add

Build credibility with laboratory teams by connecting to their clinical, technical and operational needs.
Help prospective customers assess what adoption would involve, using your knowledge of assay implementation, validation and the path to routine use.
Address buying concerns about CAP/CLIA requirements, documentation and implementation timelines with an understanding of how clinical laboratories work.
Partner with sales colleagues to answer technical and operational questions and help customers move towards a confident, informed buying decision.

Requirements

We know that every background is different, but to be best set for success we see you bringing:

Hands-on wet-lab experience with NGS workflows in a clinical laboratory.
An understanding of how clinical laboratories operate beyond the bench, including the steps needed to introduce and validate a new assay.
Substantial exposure to CAP/CLIA requirements and inspection processes, with enough involvement to explain their practical impact on laboratory work.
Experience of assay implementation or validation that helps you understand the challenges laboratories face before going live.
Willingness to travel for a customer-facing role.

You do not need to have held a customer-facing role, or previously worked as an SME or field applications specialist, but it is helpful. A desire to work in a commercialsed environment as part of a sales and solutions team is critical.

Benefits

You will be joining an organization with the patient at the heart of every decision and action, driven by purpose as we pursue exponential growth.

For more information about our Benefits, Virtues, The Recruitment Process, our AI guide and stories from our team about what it's like to work at SOPHiA, view the full posting on our careers page.

Location: Remote - Home Office in Territory (West Coast)

Contract: Permanent

new_jobs.title: Manager, People Analytics & Data Science
new_jobs.description:
Position Summary

Mercury is building a connected, trusted people analytics capability that puts decision-ready data and insights in the hands of leaders when and where they need them. The Manager, People Analytics & Data Science will help build that capability from the data foundation through the leader experience.

This role will build reliable data pipelines and analytical datasets, establish trusted metric definitions, and deliver robust dashboards that enable self-service people data for Mercury leaders. The role will also conduct targeted research and advanced analysis—including predictive and AI-enabled methods where appropriate—to surface new insights on workforce risks, capacity, performance, productivity, and other priorities.

The successful candidate will combine technical depth with strong business judgment. They will be able to move from a business question to a data model, from a data model to a clear dashboard, and from an observed pattern to a well-supported recommendation. This is a builder role for someone who wants to make people data easier to trust, easier to use, and more useful in the flow of business decisions.

Geo-Salary Information

An in-person interview may be required during the hiring process

State specific pay scales for this role are as follows:

$128,136 to $252,194 (NJ, NY, WA, HI, AK, MD, CT, RI, MA)

$116,487 to $229,267 (NV, OR, AZ, CO, WY, TX, ND, MN, MO, IL, WI, FL, GA, MI, OH, VA, PA, DE, VT, NH, ME)

$104,839 to $206,340 (UT, ID, MT, NM, SD, NE, KS, OK, IA, AR, LA, MS, AL, TN, KY, IN, SC, NC, WV)

In CA: Typical hiring range is $171,148 to $209,181

The expected base salary for this position will vary depending on a number of factors, including relevant experience, skills and location.

Responsibilities

Data foundation and analytics engineering

Partner with data engineers to design, build, and maintain reliable data pipelines and analytical datasets that bring together people, organizational, operational, and business data from relevant sources.
Develop reusable data models, transformations, validation checks, documentation, and monitoring that support accurate and repeatable analysis.
Partner with HR Tech, Enterprise Data Science, Data & Analytics, Finance, and other technical teams on source systems, data architecture, integrations, access, and data quality.
Translate business and People questions into clear data requirements, grains, dimensions, logic, refresh expectations, and ownership.
Establish and maintain metric contracts that document definitions, calculation logic, sources, refresh cadence, interpretation, stewardship, and action path.
Improve the reliability, transparency, privacy, and usability of people data as Mercury evolves its HRIS and broader data ecosystem.

Dashboards and self-service people data

Own the end-to-end delivery of leader-facing people data products, from discovery and prioritization through launch, adoption, and iteration.
Build robust operational and executive dashboards that connect people metrics to business and workforce outcomes.
Deliver focused dashboard experiences that help leaders answer what changed, what may be contributing, and what action to take next.
Design for self-service by developing intuitive personas, access patterns, definitions, documentation, enablement, and feedback loops.
Embed relevant people insights into existing executive reporting and operating rhythms wherever possible rather than creating disconnected destinations.
Measure usage, trust, decision relevance, and adoption; use feedback and evidence to expand, refine, or retire products.

Research, advanced analytics, and predictive insight

Conduct targeted research and analysis on prioritized questions such as attrition risk, critical-role readiness, capacity constraints, workforce planning, manager effectiveness, performance, productivity, and AI-enabled work.
Apply exploratory analysis, statistical methods, experimentation, forecasting, segmentation, and predictive modeling as appropriate to the question and data quality.
Translate complex analysis into clear findings, limitations, implications, and recommendations for People and business leaders.
Design analyses with appropriate validation, explainability, privacy protections, and bias-awareness; treat models as decision support, not a substitute for accountable human judgment.
Develop repeatable approaches for research intake, hypothesis formation, analysis, peer review, storytelling, and follow-through.
Partner with stakeholders to connect analytical findings to decisions, interventions, and measures of impact.

Partnership and capability building

Build trusted relationships with People leaders, business leaders, Finance, HR Tech, Enterprise Data Science, and other partners.
Shape and maintain an analytics roadmap that balances foundational data work, self-service products, and targeted research.
Establish practical standards for data quality, versioning, testing, documentation, access, and responsible use of people data.
Help leaders and People partners build confidence and fluency in using people metrics and insights.
Lead through influence and contribute to a high-performing, collaborative People Ops, Tech & Analytics team.

What success looks like

Leaders can access trusted people metrics in the tools and business rhythms where decisions already happen.
Core dashboards are clear, adopted, well-governed, and connected to meaningful business questions.
Data pipelines, metric definitions, and analytical products are reliable enough to support recurring decisions—not just one-time requests.
Targeted research produces new, decision-relevant insight on priority workforce questions.
The team has a scalable roadmap for expanding self-service, predictive analysis, and future HRIS-enabled analytics.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree in data science, statistics, computer science, mathematics, engineering, economics, business analytics, or a related field

Experience

7+ years of experience in data science, people analytics, analytics engineering, business intelligence, data engineering, or a related field.
Experience with People Analytics, HR data, workforce planning, talent, compensation, performance, or organizational research.
Demonstrated experience building data pipelines, analytical datasets, data models, or other reusable analytics infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience developing dashboards or self-service analytics products for business stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience applying statistical analysis, experimentation, forecasting, segmentation, or predictive modeling to complex business questions.
Demonstrated ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to senior leaders and non-technical audiences.
Strong hands-on skills with SQL and Python or R, plus experience with modern data pipelines, transformation, testing, and analytical workflows.
Experience with data modeling, semantic layers, BI tools, cloud data platforms, version control, and production-quality documentation.
Strong foundation in statistics, experimental design, causal reasoning, predictive modeling, and model evaluation.

Knowledge and Skills:

Able to distinguish between a reporting need, a diagnostic question, and a research or modeling question—and choose an appropriately rigorous solution.
Product-minded and user-centered: starts with the decision and designs the data experience around the user.
Strong storyteller who can make complex analysis clear, precise, and actionable without overstating certainty.
Highly collaborative, curious, pragmatic, and comfortable working across business and technical teams.
Strong judgment and discretion when handling confidential, sensitive, or personally identifiable People data.
Comfortable using AI and collaboration tools to improve productivity while applying responsible-use principles.
Able to build in ambiguity, establish standards without over-engineering, and continuously improve the quality of the work.

About The Company

Why choose a career at Mercury?

At Mercury, we have been guided by our purpose to help people reduce risk and overcome unexpected events for more than 60 years. We are one team with a common goal to help others. Everyone needs insurance and we can’t imagine a world without it.

Our team will encourage you to grow, make time to have fun, and work together to make great things happen. We embrace the strengths and values of each team member. We believe in having diverse perspectives where everyone is included, to serve customers from all walks of life.

We care about our people, and we mean it. We reward our talented professionals with a competitive salary, bonus potential, and a variety of benefits to help our team members reach their health, retirement, and professional goals.

Learn more about us here: https://www.mercuryinsurance.com/about/careers

Perks And Benefits

We offer many great benefits, including:

Competitive compensation
Flexibility to work from anywhere in the United States for most positions
Paid time off (vacation time, sick time, 9 paid Company holidays, volunteer hours)
Incentive bonus programs (potential for holiday bonus, referral bonus, and performance-based bonus)
Medical, dental, vision, life, and pet insurance
401 (k) retirement savings plan with company match
Engaging work environment
Promotional opportunities
Education assistance
Professional and personal development opportunities

What You Will Do

The primary functions of the Laboratory Assistant I are specimen collection, specimen handling and transport, specimen processing– including reference laboratory specimen processing and microbiology specimen processing clerical support, inventory monitoring, and assisting the Clinical Laboratory Scientist in the performance of automated, semi-automated and manual procedures in the clinical laboratory. 

Required Qualifications

Other Meets education requirements for California CPT Certification.

1 Year relevant work experience in a laboratory.
Minimum 6 months Phlebotomy experience.

Essential Functions

The position characteristics reflect the most important duties, responsibilities and competencies considered necessary to perform the essential functions of the job in a fully competent manner. They should not be considered as a detailed description of all the work requirements of the position. The characteristics of the position and standards of performance may be changed by TCMC with or without prior notice based on the needs of the organization. Maintains a safe, clean working environment, including unit based safety and infection control requirements. Perform specimen collections, includes venipuncture and capillary sticks. Process specimens received in the laboratory. This task includes specimen transport, handling, sorting, requisition entry, distribution of specimens to all laboratory sections. Centrifuge and aliquot specimens to appropriate containers. Enter blood culture bottles on the blood culture instrumentation. Answer the telephone, triage calls appropriately, take appropriate messages; review pending logs; locate samples for add on orders; look up patient reports on computer and give results to clinicians where appropriate. Assists in the Reception/Triage area of the Lab, as needed. Order tests in the LIS. Contact nursing units or physician’s offices to verify confusing incomplete or confusing orders or sample problems. Under the direct observation of the Clinical Laboratory Scientist, set up and load tests on instruments or procedures as determined by the section lead. Under the direct observation of the Clinical Laboratory Scientist, perform limited function checks and preventative maintenance on instruments and equipment. Take inventory of reagents and supplies and restock when needed; put away supplies as they are received. Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Knowledge and ability to use medical terminology, preferred.
Excellent professional communication and interpersonal skills are essential.

new_jobs.title: Chief College Laboratory Technician (Classroom) - Hunter-Bellevue School of Nursing, Hunter College
new_jobs.description:
Directs and trains other laboratory or technical personnel under general supervision and performs highly specialized work requiring significant theoretical knowledge, scientific and technical expertise, professional judgment, and insight in one of the fields of laboratory or applied science. 

May oversee multiple laboratories in a single department, or laboratories in multiple departments with a significant number of technicians. Highly specialized work may include development of research designs and fabrication, modification, repair, maintenance and operation of highly complex research or technical equipment.

Job Title Name: Chief College Laboratory Technician

CONTRACT TITLE
Chief College Laboratory Technician

FLSA
Exempt

CAMPUS SPECIFIC INFORMATION
The Hunter-Bellevue School of Nursing at Hunter College is the flagship nursing school of the City University of New York (CUNY) and cultivates collaborative nurse leaders promoting wellness and championing health equity in local and global communities through excellence in education, research, scholarship, and advocacy. The School of Nursing invites highly motivated applicants for the position of Chief College Lab Technician.
POSITION DETAILS:
Reporting to the Dean, the Chief College Lab Technician will:
•    Manage the day-to-day operations of the nursing labs, including scheduling, equipment maintenance, and inventory control.
•    Train and supervise lab personnel.
•    Enforce and implement safety protocols. 
•    Troubleshoot hardware and software issues and coordinates the maintenance and system upgrades of technology/equipment.
•    Support faculty and students in clinical teaching and simulation-based learning in nursing lab settings. 
•    Identify equipment and technology for clinical teaching and simulation-based learning.
•    Provide faculty training regarding technology and equipment.
•    Maintain currency and proficiency in related technology and software.
•    Ensure adherence to CUNY, state, and federal regulations for lab operations and safety.
•    Develop lab policies and procedures.
•    Work evenings and weekends as needed.
•    Other duties that align with the school’s mission and strategic goals. 

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
High School Diploma with a minimum of twelve years' related experience. Additional education may be used to meet the experience requirement: an Associate degree may be substituted for two years experience, a Bachelor's degree may be substituted for four years experience, and a Master's degree in an area appropriate to the duties to be performed may be substituted for an additional one year's experience. This position requires a high level of technical expertise.

OTHER QUALIFICATIONS
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
•    Bachelor’s degree or higher in nursing.
•    New York State license as a registered nurse required or following hire. 
•    Experience in a nursing or simulation lab beneficial.
•    Strong knowledge of infection control, safety, and quality procedures.
•    Proficiency in nursing skills and technology.
•    Excellent organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
•    Expertise with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint and other software systems.
•    Ability to work in a fast-paced, educational environment with attention to detail.

COMPENSATION
Salary commensurate with education and experience ($102,508 - $111,459).

CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development.

BENEFITS
CUNY offers a comprehensive benefits package to employees and eligible dependents based on job title and classification. Employees are also offered pension and Tax-Deferred Savings Plans. Part-time employees must meet a weekly or semester work hour criteria to be eligible for health benefits. Health benefits are also extended to retirees who meet the eligibility criteria.

CLOSING DATE
The search will remain open until the position is filled. The committee will begin reviewing complete applications on Oct. 19, 2026. Applications submitted after the deadline will only be considered if the position/s remain open after initial round.
